mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 750i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a BMW 750i, replacement costs vary significantly by generation. E38 750i (M73B54 V12) engines range from £1,800-£3,200 used, £3,200-£5,500 reconditioned, and £4,500-£7,500 rebuilt. E65 750i (N62B48 V8) engines range from £2,500-£4,000 used, £4,000-£6,500 reconditioned, and £5,500-£8,500 rebuilt. F01 750i (N63B44) engines range from £3,500-£7,000 used, £6,000-£11,000 reconditioned, and £8,000-£14,000 rebuilt. G11 750i (N63B44C/D) engines range from £4,500-£9,000 used, £7,500-£14,000 reconditioned, and £10,000-£18,000 rebuilt. Labour adds approximately £1,000-£1,500 for specialist fitment.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N63 hot restart failure in a BMW 750i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptom is the engine cranking but not starting when hot, particularly after a short stop. The check engine light may illuminate after a hot engine restart. The problem is caused by air in the cooling system collecting in the area of the turbocharger electric coolant pump. This is a well-documented issue affecting N63 engines in the 750i.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 750i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and value. For an E38 750i worth under £4,000, consider repair or a used engine rather than a full rebuild. For E65 750is worth £4,000-£8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine typically justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. For F01 750is worth £8,000-£15,000, rebuilt engines make sense if the car is otherwise in excellent condition. For G11 750is worth £15,000+, replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. If the car is otherwise in excellent condition, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components can extend its life by 80,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 750i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 750i engine replacements take 3-5 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The V8 and V12 engine complexity - particularly on N63 twin-turbo units - means careful removal and installation is essential. V12 M73 engines are also labour-intensive due to engine bay packaging. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 24-72 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 7 Series 750i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 750i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with 3-6 month warranties, while reconditioned units usually include 6-12 month cover. Extended warranty options are available on most rebuilt units, particularly important for complex N63 V8 engines.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M73, N62, and N63 engines in the BMW 750i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M73 is a 5.4-litre naturally aspirated V12 producing 326hp, fitted to E38 750is from 1994-2001. The N62 is a 4.8-litre naturally aspirated V8 producing 367hp, fitted to E65 750is from 2002-2008. The N63 is a 4.4-litre twin-turbocharged V8 producing 407-530hp, fitted to F01 (2008-2015) and G11 (2015-present) 750is. The N63 is the most powerful but also the most complex, with additional failure points including turbochargers, high-pressure fuel pumps, and hot restart issues not present on the M73 or N62.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 7 Series 750i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 750i debuted in the E32 generation in 1987 as the flagship V12 model. The name continued through the E38 with a 5.4-litre V12, then transitioned to a V8 for the E65 and subsequent generations. The 750i has evolved from a naturally aspirated 12-cylinder to a twin-turbo V8 producing over 520hp in its most potent form.

milestones.description: M70B50, 5.0L V12, 300hp - launched in E32 750i (first BMW V12)
N62B48, 4.8L V8, 367hp - E65 750i launch (V12 replaced by V8)
N63B44B, 4.4L twin-turbo V8, 449hp - F01 LCI update
N63B44D, 4.4L twin-turbo V8, 530hp - G11 LCI update

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 7 Series 750i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 750i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 750i has worn four very different engines over its lifetime. The E38's M73 V12 is widely considered the most reliable of the generation. The E65's N62 V8 suffers primarily from valve stem seal failure. The F01 and G11's N63 twin-turbo V8 engines are the most complex and failure-prone, with hot restart issues, timing chain stretch, and turbocharger failures being common. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Valve Stem Seal Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 750i N62 Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: The rubber valve stem seals harden and crack with age and heat exposure, losing their ability to seal the valve guide. Oil seeps into the combustion chamber and burns, producing blue smoke from the exhaust, particularly noticeable when idling in traffic. Forum reports show failure as early as 69,500 miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all valve stem seals using specialist tooling (AGA tool set)
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if engine otherwise healthy and car worth £4,000+
Best for higher-mileage units with multiple concurrent failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E65 750i (2002-2008) is worth £2,500-£8,000. For cars valued under £4,000, valve stem seal replacement may still be viable if the car is otherwise in good condition. For cars worth £4,000-£8,000, a rebuilt or reconditioned engine typically justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: If your N62 750i has blue smoke on startup but runs well otherwise, specialist valve stem seal replacement is a sensible investment. If the engine has high mileage and other issues (cooling system, timing chain wear), a rebuilt engine with upgraded components may be the better long-term choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N62B48 BMW 7 Series 750i engine prices

problems.h4: N63 Hot Restart Issue - BMW 7 Series 750i Won't Start When Hot
problems.rootCause: Air in the cooling system collects in the area of the turbocharger electric coolant pump. When the engine is shut off, the turbocharger coolant pump impeller continues to spin down in the air pocket, preventing proper cooling. This causes the engine to crank but not start when hot. The check engine light may illuminate after a hot restart.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Bleed cooling system, inspect electric coolant pump
Supply & fit, upgraded cooling system components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if hot restart has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical F01 750i (2008-2015) is worth £5,000-£15,000. A typical G11 750i (2015-present) is worth £12,000-£40,000. For G11 750is, replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. For F01 750is, evaluate carefully - a £6,000-£10,000 engine on a £5,000 car may not be cost-effective.
problems.recommendation: The N63 hot restart issue is a known design weakness. If your 750i experiences this, have the cooling system inspected immediately. If the engine has been repeatedly overheated or the issue has been ignored, internal damage is likely - a rebuilt engine with upgraded components is the only reliable solution.

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Turbocharger Failure - BMW 7 Series 750i N63 Engine
problems.rootCause: Early N63 engines suffer from timing chain stretch due to heat-soaked components. Turbocharger failures are caused by oil supply line blockage, leading to bearing starvation. The hot-vee architecture means heat damages components in ways not seen on traditional V8 layouts.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before engine damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed turbocharger unit, inspect oil supply
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if only one turbo failed and oil system clear

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing and turbo components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if multiple failures or engine has internal damage

problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling on cold start or experience turbocharger failure on your N63 750i, have the timing chain and oil supply system inspected immediately. Early replacement of the chain and guides can save the engine. If the chain has already failed causing internal damage, or both turbos are failing, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing and turbo components is the only reliable solution.
